title: Recursive Decentralized Collaborative Localization for Sparsely Communicating Robots
authors: Lukas Luft | Tobias Schubert | Stergios I. Roumeliotis | Wolfram Burgard
locator: Section IV, Fig. 2, Table II, ref. 15
evidence_or_scope: Nine MR.CLAM sequences from five robots are replayed; rotating which robot observes landmarks yields five dependent reuses per sequence. Dropping bearings or substituting simulated relative poses changes the input. Paired radio transmission and receipt are not reported.

version_note: Related 2018 journal work 10.1177/0278364918760698; shared source data.

title: Learning-Based Measurement Scheduling for Loosely-Coupled Cooperative Localization
evidence_or_scope: Five indoor robots; the scheduling simulation uses MR.CLAM subsets separate from training and limits each agent to at most four inter-agent measurements per timestep. It tests which measurements to process; physical send/receive timing is unreported.

evidence_or_scope: Authors report NTP inter-vehicle clock error 2.0 ms mean (SD 8.9 ms) and network packet delay 84.0 ms mean (SD 71.4 ms). These are aggregate observations in their own platform and do not reconstruct MR.CLAM packets.

title: Don’t Fire Together: Desynchronised Communication Scheduling for Bandwidth-Limited Multi-Robot Exploration
authors: Rong Zhao | Haohua Que | Jiajun Sun | Jiayue Xie | Qian Zhang | Fei Qiao
evidence_level: full text, publisher version via Europe PMC
evidence_or_scope: One monitor timestamps arrivals for four differential-drive robots; peak summed staleness drops from 15.8 s to 10.5 s in one paired comparison. A second four-robot fleet has five paired runs; peak staleness drops from 15.9 s to 10.0 s. These metrics do not establish one-way packet latency or a reliable task-travel gain.
rights_and_data: Article CC BY 4.0. Data/code statement offers reasonable request and promises public release; no independently verified trial files in this review.

title: Cooperative Localization Approach for Multi-Robot Systems Based on State Estimation Error Compensation
evidence_level: full text, publisher version via Europe PMC
evidence_or_scope: The model distinguishes the transmitted estimate/measurement at t3 from receipt at t4. The worked simulation assumes constant 0.1 s communication delay and 0.8 s filtering period; this is no empirical trace of wireless latency.
rights_and_data: Article CC BY 4.0; no raw timestamps distributed.

title: Scalable Edge–Cloud Cooperative Digital Twin Control for Multi-Robot Systems
authors: Daniel Poul Mtowe | Minhyeok Park | Dong Min Kim
locator: Table 3 and preceding synchronization-latency paragraph; Data Availability
evidence_or_scope: Each tested fleet size has one continuous 1200 s run and more than 13,400 acknowledged observation updates. With unsynchronised observer/server clocks, uplink latency is estimated as half of application RTT assuming approximate path symmetry. Frame statistics share a run.
rights_and_data: Article CC BY 4.0; availability statement points to article and corresponding author. No public per-packet trace verified.
